mind_mode::Modes::decide in crates/yantrik-ui/src/mind_mode.rs and decide()
in deploy/yantrik-os/yos-mcp are the same table written twice, on purpose:
the bridge deciding for itself costs one read of the shell instead of two.
Two copies drift. These vectors are what stops it being silent — the Rust
side writes them and a test asserts the file still matches; the Python side
is driven through every one of them by yos-mcp-selftest.py.
layer: `shell` came straight out of Modes::decide. `harness_cap` is
YOS_MCP_MAX_PERMISSION, which the shell does not enforce and should not —
it is a cap a harness puts on itself — and `browser` is the plan-mode rule
for tools that are not on the shell's surface at all. Both are modelled in
the generator, which the generator says so about.
unrecoverable is approvals::unrecoverable over the action's own published
purpose, and it is an INPUT to both tables since 21 September 2026: in auto
an action the app says cannot be undone is asked about exactly as a
dangerous one is, and no session rule covers one in any mode. It was
carried and ignored before that, under the name `recoverable`, which is why
the axis was already here to turn on. safe is excluded: a read destroys
nothing, so matching wording cannot make one into a question.
Since 28 September 2026 bypass asks about such an action too, and
bypass_all (Full bypass) is the one mode that runs it unasked.
open_ended is approvals::open_ended over the same purpose: the action runs
whatever it is given (gate::OPEN_ENDED, since 29 September 2026). Above
safe it asks in ask, auto and bypass, and a session rule covers it;
bypass_all runs it and plan refuses it. Where both are said,
unrecoverable wins.
